alex (support): heads-up — two enterprise customers (acme-co, betahealth) opened escalations: sudden p95/p99 latency regressions on text-generation endpoints after last runtime push. They see p99s > 1s for short prompts that used to be ~120ms. :grimacing:

maria (eng-runtime): ack. which build / deploy? any correlation with kernel/attention flags?

alex (support): deploy-bot shows runtime v2.34.2 rolled out yesterday 23:15 UTC. deploy-bot: 
```
deploy-bot: started deploy runtime/v2.34.2 -> prod (canary 10%)
deploy-bot: canary healthy -> promote 50% -> 100%
```

sam (eng-ml): I pushed a change in the compiler flags and default kernel selection for Ampere nodes in that release — enabled FlashAttention2 and set kernel_selection = "auto". Also added SDPA fallback for some sequence lengths. Possible fallback thrashing?

jordan (eng-sre): metric dump from datadog (shortened):
```
- endpoint: /v1/generate/text
- p50: 85ms -> 90ms
- p95: 120ms -> 520ms
- p99: 240ms -> 1100ms
- cpu_time: +30% on host kernel process
- kernel_time (gpu): +2x for some requests
```

maria (eng-runtime): that smells like a kernel selection problem where FlashAttention hits a bad codepath and falls back on SDPA or a slow kernel for certain cls/seq combos. we saw similar before with very long prompts, but customers said prompts are short (~40 tokens).

sam (eng-ml): right — I looked at the perf traces. For short sequences we pick FlashAttention kernels; however if KV cache hit patterns differ we sometimes end up switching to a different kernel per step which invalidates some caches and spikes latency. here's the trace snippet from the perf tool: 
```
TRACE: request_id=R-8943
step 1: flash_attn_fwd (0.9ms)
step 2: sdpa_fwd (35ms)  <-- slow fallback
step 3: flash_attn_fwd (1.1ms)
```

alex (support): we also have a couple of reproducible customer traces — uploading below. They repro locally on our dedicated test cluster when we pin to v2.34.2.

maria (eng-runtime): can you paste the minimal repro curl for the test cluster?

alex (support): yup — on the repro cluster (internal):
```
curl -X POST https://repro.internal.redwood/v1/generate \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"rwd-small-v1","input":"Summarize: The quick brown fox...","max_tokens":60}'
```
Response times: 95ms, 1.2s, 88ms, 1.1s (alternating).

jordan (eng-sre): alternating pattern -> kernel thrash. good find. mitigation options: 1) toggle FlashAttention off globally, 2) change kernel_selection to prefer "reference" kernel for a short window, 3) hotfix to pin compile flag to previous behavior and redeploy.

maria (eng-runtime): can we do a targeted runtime config flip on the problematic pool (ampere-prod-*) instead of global? prefer local rollback first.

sam (eng-ml): yes — runtime supports per-pool kernel overrides. we can set: 
```json
{"pools": {"ampere-prod-1": {"kernel_selection": "prefer_reference", "flash_attn_enabled": false}}}
```
Use redwoodctl to patch live config: 
```bash
redwoodctl runtime patch --pool ampere-prod-1 --set 'flash_attn_enabled=false' --set 'kernel_selection=prefer_reference'
```
I'll prepare the exact command.

maria (eng-runtime): please prepare the command and I'll run it in canary and monitor p95/p99 before promoting. also add a metric viz for kernel-change events.

deploy-bot: rollback candidate detected (runtime/v2.34.1) — manual promote required. :information_source: 

alex (support): customers asked for ETA on fix — suggested telling them we're investigating and a potential config hotfix within 2 hours. lily (customer-success) drafting comms.

lily (customer-success): I can send a holding message: "We're investigating a latency regression affecting some generation calls. Engineering is testing a targeted runtime config change now. We'll update within 2 hours with an expected fix or workaround." ok? :thumbsup: 

maria (eng-runtime): executing targeted flip on canary pool now. running command: 
```bash
# run by maria
redwoodctl runtime patch --pool ampere-canary-3 --set 'flash_attn_enabled=false' --set 'kernel_selection=prefer_reference' --reason 'hotfix for p99 regression'
```

ops-bot: config patch applied to ampere-canary-3 by maria at 2026-03-15T01:12:10Z

jordan (eng-sre): metrics after patch (canary): p95 130ms, p99 210ms — much better. running 30m smoke.

sam (eng-ml): confirms local repro against canary: alternating pattern gone. codepath now consistently hits reference kernel. perf traces: 
```
TRACE: request_id=R-8943
step 1: reference_attn_fwd (4.5ms)
step 2: reference_attn_fwd (4.6ms)
step 3: reference_attn_fwd (4.2ms)
```

maria (eng-runtime): good. plan: promote the config flip to all ampere-prod pools as a hotfix (no full redeploy) and open a follow-up to revert the compile/kernel change or make FlashAttention more conservative (sequence-length thresholds). sam, can you own the code fix? jordan will own the rollout, i'll own the monitoring and postmortem.

sam (eng-ml): will do. immediate follow-ups: add a failsafe to disable flashattn when thrashing is detected (kernel switch count > 3 in N steps). also add unit perf tests for 8-64 token range.

maria (eng-runtime): executing promote to prod pools now (rolling):
```bash
redwoodctl runtime patch --pool ampere-prod-1 --set 'flash_attn_enabled=false' --set 'kernel_selection=prefer_reference' --reason 'hotfix p99 regression'
redwoodctl runtime patch --pool ampere-prod-2 --set 'flash_attn_enabled=false' --set 'kernel_selection=prefer_reference' --reason 'hotfix p99 regression'
# ...
```

ops-bot: patches applied to ampere-prod-* by maria at 2026-03-15T01:38:07Z

jordan (eng-sre): prod metrics now (10m window): p95 140ms (baseline ~120ms), p99 260ms (down from 1.1s). alerting thresholds cleared. monitoring for 2h.

alex (support): customers updated — two replied saying latency looks normal now on their end. re-checking tickets and will close if stable.

lily (customer-success): sending update to customers with note about hotfix and that engineering will follow up with a permanent fix.

maria (eng-runtime): postmortem checklist:
- [ ] sam to open PR to make FlashAttention opt-in per-model with conservative thresholds and add thrash detection (owner: sam)
- [ ] eng-runtime to add canary perf suite that runs generation p50/p95/p99 on 8/16/32/64 token workloads before promoting (owner: maria)
- [ ] eng-sre to add alert for kernel-switch-rate > 2 per request (owner: jordan)
- [ ] ship rollback/revert plan in next patch release notes (owner: maria)
- [ ] customer success follow-ups (owner: lily)

sam (eng-ml): opened ticket #ENGML-3581 with proposed fixes and PR will be up today. also adding compile guard so FlashAttention default remains off for now while we iterate.

maria (eng-runtime): thanks all. closing thread for now — will re-open if we see new regressions. great collaboration. :clap:

deploy-bot: runtime/v2.34.2 remains in registry; next deploy will include sam's fix or we can revert to v2.34.1 per release lead decision.

alex (support): closing loop with customers and will attach thread perf charts to each ticket.

jordan (eng-sre): leaving monitoring playbook entry: if p99 > 800ms and kernel_switch_count spike then run: 
```bash
# emergency steps
redwoodctl runtime patch --pool <pool> --set 'flash_attn_enabled=false' --set 'kernel_selection=prefer_reference'
redwoodctl route update --fallback-model rwd-small-v1-ref
```

maria (eng-runtime): nice. end."
